source.title: Neural scaling laws for phenotypic drug discovery
source.authors: Drew A. Linsley; J. Griffin; Jason Brown; Adam N. Roose; Michael J. Frank; Peter Linsley; Steven Finkbeiner; Jeremy W. Linsley

record.tranche_reason: The study reports scaling results for image-based drug-discovery models and finds that they depend on the training objective and data regime: IBP-pretrained models improve with added data, while task-supervised models do not scale consistently. This refines the scope of scaling claims, though it does not test language-model cross-entropy laws.
record.gate_note: The study reports downstream Pheno-CA performance scaling for image-based DNNs, which bears on V5–V7. Results cited from prior work and the compound-discovery comparison with Cell Profiler are not rows because they do not report a scaling result. No result measures held-out language-model pretraining loss or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
record.test_reason: The study brings scaling to a new setting: residual-MLP DNNs on Cell Profiler features from cell-painting screens, scored on downstream drug-discovery probes. It fits data-scaling laws for IBP-pretrained models and reports that task-supervised models do not scale. That is a result on V5 (other training regimes and modalities) in a new domain, so T3 rather than T5. It does not measure language-model pretraining loss, compute-optimal allocation or extrapolation accuracy.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that IBP-pretrained DNNs outperform task-supervised ones and follow linear data-scaling laws on Pheno-CA tasks, and that they improve with parameter count while depth effects are unclear. Task-supervised DNNs do not scale. Reaching 100% MoA accuracy would need about 3.25M more compounds, which is impractical, so new experimental methods are needed.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses image-based cell-phenotype DNNs, an inverse-biological-process precursor task, frozen representations, and task probes. It measures downstream classification accuracy and categorical cross-entropy against data and model scale, rather than language-model held-out pretraining loss or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: Results differ between IBP pretraining and direct task supervision; replicate amount changes average MoA performance and the data-scaling slope; model depth affects performance, with 9-layer models outperforming 12-layer models on MoA and target tasks; plotted MoA and target curves decline at their high-data ends.
record.problems: The reported scaling relations are for downstream phenotypic tasks in a single image-based drug-discovery setting, not language-model pretraining loss. The scaling slopes are reported without uncertainty estimates in the text. Some downturns and curve details are available only in figures. Results also vary by training objective, replicate amount, and architecture.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. The compound-discovery comparison with Cell Profiler and cited results from other studies were not included because they do not report the scaling outcomes covered by the tested versions.

untested.parts: The study projects 3.25M more compounds needed for 100% MoA accuracy, but never checks any extrapolation against larger runs.
No fixed-parameter comparison of shapes; depth and width vary together with parameter count.
No power-law fit of loss, no compute axis, and no repeated-data or fine-tuning law. The data range is only about 2 orders of magnitude.
No language-model downstream tasks; the downstream probe results are recorded under V5.
No parameter-counting, schedule or fitting-method comparisons; no comparison of published exponents.

missing.what: Extrapolated projection from the MoA linear law: about 3.25M more compounds (about 14M images) for 100% accuracy. It is not validated, but it is the study's use of the law to predict far beyond the fitted range.

record.verdict_notes: The models are residual MLPs on PCA-whitened Cell Profiler well vectors, not raw-image models, and all are small (at most 12 layers, 1512 width). The measures are downstream probe accuracy or probe cross-entropy; no pretraining-loss scaling is reported. The scaling fits use the maximum-performing models per curve, and slopes are given without uncertainty. The reader's V6 links were moved to V5, because this non-language setting falls under V5 and V6 is about language-model downstream tasks. The text's cross-references to figures are inconsistent.

versions.untested_parts: No language-model held-out pretraining loss, or power-law fit in parameters, tokens, or compute, is measured.
No small-run fit is evaluated against much larger language-model runs.
No fixed-compute allocation between parameters and tokens is tested.
The study varies depth and feature width in image-based DNNs, but does not compare held-out loss at a fixed parameter count or test the claim about language-model architecture details.

Tests image-based DNNs on phenotypic drug-discovery tasks, including IBP pretraining and replicate variation. It does not test video or other modalities, language-model pretraining loss, or fine-tuning and transfer regimes beyond frozen IBP representations with task probes.
Tests downstream Pheno-CA performance against data and model scale. It does not test downstream performance as a function of language-model pretraining loss or performance on language-model tasks.

Reports dependence on task objective, replicate amount, and architecture, plus curve downturns described as overfitting. It does not estimate language-model exponents or a compute-optimal split, nor systematically vary parameter counting, training schedule, or fitting method.

rows.value: Linear scaling law; performance increases by 1% with approximately 56K (non-unique) OOD molecules added for training.

It covers only about 2 orders of magnitude (1e3–1e5 molecules) and is fitted to the max-performing models per curve. The record does not say the measure is probe accuracy rather than pretraining loss. V6 removed: V6 concerns language-model downstream tasks.
